sources.title: Qdrant
sources.purpose: Compared in every vector test, pinned by image digest. Also the capability the owner wants triggered dynamically through a knowledge path.

sources.title: Milvus
sources.purpose: Compared in every vector test, pinned by image digest.

sources.title: SurrealDB
sources.purpose: Compared in every vector test, pinned by image digest. Version 3.3.5 stays beside version 4.0.0, released on 2026-11-03, so the new major version's effect can be read directly.

sources.title: LanceDB
sources.purpose: Compared in every vector test through eval/lab/lance_system.py, locked by hash.

sources.title: Lance format and engine
sources.purpose: The engine beneath LanceDB, locked with it.

sources.title: VectorDBBench
sources.purpose: Run against Qdrant, Milvus and LanceDB as a cross-check on this lab, and imported with rrflow-lab import. Driving RRFlow from inside it needs a client patch, which is a next step.

sources.title: ANN-Benchmarks
sources.purpose: Its published datasets come in through eval/lab/import_corpus.py. Its harness is not run.

sources.title: COCO image embeddings, 512 dimensions, angular
sources.license: COCO's terms: annotations CC BY 4.0, images under Flickr's terms
sources.purpose: Real embeddings for vector-coco-i2i.json, listed in ANN-Benchmarks' dataset table. Used for local benchmarking only, and not stored in this repository. Its published neighbors were computed at lower precision, so the lab grades with its own exact answers.

sources.title: Big ANN Benchmarks
sources.purpose: Has filtered, streaming, sparse and out-of-distribution tracks, which this lab does not yet exercise.

sources.title: Qdrant's benchmark harness
sources.purpose: A vendor's harness, useful for comparing how filtered search is measured.

sources.title: Inspect
sources.purpose: Candidate for task definitions and logs in the reasoning tests, imported into this report rather than replacing it.

sources.title: promptfoo
sources.purpose: Prompt-level comparison from configuration files. It suits regression checks better than agent task grading.

sources.title: MLflow
sources.purpose: Tracking and evaluation platform. Its results could be imported if an owner workflow uses it.

sources.title: Arize Phoenix
sources.purpose: Tracing and evaluation. Its Elastic License 2.0 is not an OSI-approved license, so read its terms before any use.

sources.title: DeepEval
sources.purpose: Agent and retrieval metrics. Its model-graded metrics would need an independent check.

sources.title: Ragas
sources.purpose: Retrieval metrics. Its last release was 2026-01-13, so check it is still maintained before use.

sources.title: Awesome REA
sources.purpose: The owner's list of AI reverse-engineering work, watched here for new tools, cases with mechanical checks, and controlled studies. Its value to this lab is its evidence, not its app list.

sources.title: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)
sources.purpose: A planned arm in the reasoning tests, installed only in an isolated host environment, and pointed only at targets we may analyze. It is not needed to study Qdrant, Milvus, Lance or SurrealDB, whose source can be read.

sources.title: leanrea
sources.purpose: A planned arm in the reasoning tests: one skill file and plain commands. Its author reports matching REA's accuracy at 35% less cost on 36 runs.

sources.title: rea-lab
sources.purpose: Five preregistered studies, 482 runs. Offering agents REA did not significantly raise solve rates and took about twice the time and cost. A model for the reasoning tests' design, and a source of known-answer tasks, including tasks on programs published after a model's training data.

sources.title: MERIT: When Does Memory Help?
sources.purpose: 23,440 scored episodes grading memory by task success and cost. It found agents acted on a correctly retrieved value only 55% of the time, so the reasoning tests must separate what was retrieved from what was used.

sources.title: Ground Truth First
sources.purpose: A longitudinal instrument for agent memory. Only its title and abstract listing have been seen so far.

sources.title: LoCoMo, LongMemEval and BEAM, as surveyed by Mem0
sources.purpose: Recall benchmarks for agent memory. This survey comes from a vendor, and its scores are that vendor's own. Newer suites grade actions, which suits planning better.
